# Proving you're human shouldn't require an eyeball scanner. | André F. · LinkedIn · 2026-04-06

**André F.**: Founder and CEO at Incognia for 5 years 11 months with 15 years 1 month of total professional experience. Previous roles include CEO and Founder at In Loco and Founder and CEO at ubee. Based in San Francisco Bay Area [US].

---

Proving you're human shouldn't require an eyeball scanner.

Most proof of humanity solutions go straight to biometrics. Scan an iris, get a credential.

But a credential ages the moment it's captured.

It can be handed off. It can be spoofed. And it only tells you who someone was at the moment they scanned, not who controls the account today.

We think the stronger signal has been there the whole time.

Real people have homes.
They have routines.
They commute, sleep, and run errands.

Over weeks and months, those behaviors create a physical signature that's statistically unique and nearly impossible to fake at scale.

A device farm running 10,000 accounts can't generate 10,000 distinct, internally consistent location histories going back months.

A bot doesn't have a morning commute.

Today we're introducing the Physical Presence Score, a continuous, privacy-preserving attestation that a device is held by a real, unique human moving through the real world.

No orb, no enrollment, nothing asked of the user.

We already have 1B+ devices in our network. The leading biometric alternative only has 18 million users, limited to locations with physical hardware.

Our false acceptance rate is 1 in 17 million. This is 10x to 100x better than iris recognition benchmarks from NIST.

The score is built on four signals:

1. Behavioral location uniqueness
→ A real person's movement creates a physical signature that's statistically unique

2. Co-presence detection
→ Devices clustering at the same location flag coordinated fraud

3. Device liveness and integrity
→ Confirms a real device moving through the real world

4. Behavioral continuity over time
→ Refreshed continuously, so anomalies surface the moment behavior shifts

We're working with early integration partners now.

If distinguishing real users from synthetic ones is a problem you're actively trying to solve, reach out to the team.
